question.prompt: Define a function on the positive integers recursively by \(f(1)=2,\) \(f(n)=f(n-1)+1\) if \(n\) is even, and \(f(n)=f(n-2)+2\) if \(n\) is odd and greater than \(1.\) What is \(f(2017)?\)

solutions.title: Find and verify a formula
solutions.explanation:
The first few values are
\[
f(1)=2,\quad f(2)=3,\quad f(3)=4,\quad f(4)=5,
\]
suggesting that \(f(n)=n+1\).

To verify this pattern, let \(g(n)=n+1\). Its initial value is \(g(1)=2\). For even \(n\),
\[
g(n-1)+1=n+1=g(n).
\]
For odd \(n>1\),
\[
g(n-2)+2=(n-1)+2=n+1=g(n).
\]
Thus \(g\) satisfies both recursive rules. Because each rule determines a value from an earlier input, the initial value and recursion uniquely determine the function. Therefore \(f(n)=n+1\), so
\[
\boxed{f(2017)=2018}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{B}\).
